evidence_quotes.quote: Distribution of Asellus aquaticus and microinvertebrates in a non-chlorinated drinking water supply system - Effects of pipe material and sedimentation
Danish drinking water supplies based on ground water without chlorination were investigated for the presence of the water louse, Asellus aquaticus, microinvertebrates (<2 mm) and annelida.
The frequency of A. aquaticus was significantly higher in cast iron pipes than in plastic pipes.

raw_response.plain_vs_narrow_note: Excluded under both narrow and plain Criterion 2 readings because the study is purely a technical/biological drinking-water distribution engineering investigation with no legal, administrative, regulatory, institutional, or governance dimension.
raw_response.rationale: Purely technical water-distribution engineering and biological monitoring study examining the occurrence of Asellus aquaticus and microinvertebrates in Danish drinking water pipes and elevated tanks as a function of physical factors (centrifugal pumps, cast iron vs. plastic pipe material, and sediment volume), with no household service access outcome or legal/administrative mechanism (E06).
